question: does compact/SoA AST representation reduce Go memory (language-agnostic check)?
workload: binary-expr tree with identifier leaves + Loc, isomorphic to esbuild AST (Expr{Data interface,Loc}; EBinary{Left,Right,Op})
fidelity: microbench sizeof matches real esbuild: Expr=24 EBinary=56 ECall=56 EIdent=12 Loc=4 Ref=8 (verified via go run in /root/esbuild)
method: independent process per variant, runtime.ReadMemStats after GC with sink holding result; GOMAXPROCS=1; 3 sizes
finding: Compact representation cuts Go AST memory 4.4x (88 -> 20 B/node), stable across 100k/1M/4M scale.
Benefit is language-agnostic: bottleneck is 'interface + per-node heap alloc', not Go-vs-TS.
B (flat struct, no interface) and C (SoA) are IDENTICAL at 20B — the win comes from removing interface indirection + per-node allocation, NOT from SoA layout itself.
esbuild's Loc is already a value type (4B inline) unlike TS (32B heap object), so Go starts ahead; yet interface+node-alloc still costs 88B.
caveat: This isolates AST node storage only; real bundle memory also has source buffer, strings, symbol tables, GC churn. A 4.4x node reduction is an upper bound on what representation change alone can save.
